messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: p99 latency breach detected on dedicated pool north-1-dedicated-42. p99=3.2s (SLO=1.5s) over last 5m. queue_depth=212, warmup_fail_rate=17%. Streaming stalls reported. Paging oncall @Rita Chen :rotating_light:
Rita Chen: oncall here. seeing the alert, pulling pool health and autoscaler events now. initial hypothesis: warmup handshake lag causing requests to pile up -> queue amplification.
Sam Patel: I can help with pool logs and tracing. which customers hit this?
Rita Chen: cs reported a handful of mid-tier customers with streaming stalls and tail-end token spikes. Jamie from CS pinged earlier.
Jamie (cs): Confirmed: 3 customers reported degraded streaming and occasional truncated responses. Started ~11:02 UTC, high variance around 11:05.
Alex Kim: grabbing autoscaler metrics. metric snapshot:
```
autoscaler.scale_attempts: 12 in last 10m
autoscaler.success_rate: 66%
pool.available_slots: 2/24
pool.warm_pods: 6
pool.cold_pods_boot_time_p50: 38s
handshake_latency_p95: 950ms
```

Maya Ops: That's nasty. Warmup p50=38s explains why new capacity didn't absorb burst. Are warmup hooks failing?
Rita Chen: checking warmup logs now. Command:
```
rcli pool tail north-1-dedicated-42 --lines 200 --filter warmup
```
Output shows repeated `handshake timeout` at ~11:03:10 and several `gpu-init` steps hanging ~30-45s.
Jordan (eng-runtime): We're seeing kernel selection hangs on some nodes once they start swapping quantized kernels for vjaz. Could be a driver/firmware regression in the latest runtime image that slows container readiness. Rolling deploy to canary noted 2:40 UTC this morning.
Sam Patel: If runtime image is slower to initialize, autoscaler will think nodes are ready later and queue will grow. Need quick mitigation: 1) divert traffic away from affected pool, 2) force warm pool of pre-warmed nodes, 3) rollback runtime canary if necessary.
Rita Chen: Agreed. Initiating traffic routing policy to move new requests to north-2 and fallback pools for compatible model variants. Command: `rcli routing set --pool north-1-dedicated-42 --weight 0.15 --fallback north-2-dedicated-*`
Alex Kim: Done. Observability: queue depth dropped from 212 -> 80 in ~45s after reroute. p99 improved to 1.9s but still above SLO.
Maya Ops: Requesting temporary scale override to add 6 pre-warmed slots to north-1 to handle in-flight sessions. `rcli pool prewarm north-1-dedicated-42 --count 6 --profile fast`
Rita Chen: Prewarm issued. Also flagged pool nodes with `runtime:v2.9.1-canary` image for rollback. Jordan, can you coordinate rollback?
Jordan (eng-runtime): On it. Initiating controlled rollback of the canary to v2.8.8 on a subset of nodes. Using orchestrator patch to avoid full drain. Command: `orch patch --pool north-1-dedicated-42 --image runtime:v2.8.8 --max-unavailable 3`
Sam Patel: Noted. Also enabling aggressive KV prefix cache on north-1 to reduce warmup token cost for active keys: `rcli cache adjust --pool north-1-dedicated-42 --prefix-ttl 1800 --hotset-size 1.5GB`
Rita Chen: Live metrics: p95=820ms, p99=1.6s after reroute + prewarm. Streaming stall incidents reported falling to near-zero. CS confirms fewer customer errors.
Jamie (cs): Customer A reports streaming resumed. They saw ~20% degraded requests during the 11:00-11:10 window. They're asking for postmortem and RCA.
Maya Ops: Capturing timeline for postmortem:
- 10:58 UTC: minor increase in request rate for a handful of customers
- 11:02 UTC: autoscaler attempted scale-up (12 attempts)
- 11:03 UTC: handshake timeouts begin (warmup p50 jumps)
- 11:05 UTC: p99 breaches 3s, incident-bot pages oncall
- 11:07 UTC: reroute to north-2 and prewarm issued
- 11:13 UTC: rollback initiated for runtime canary on subset
- 11:25 UTC: p99 back to ~1.2s, customers report service restoration
Rita Chen: Next actions: 1) keep rollback until we validate full end-to-end warmup path 2) run a canary with extra instrumentation to capture `gpu-init`/`kernel-select` timing 3) update autoscaler heuristics to account for longer container init times (increase handshake timeout threshold and prefer prewarm when p50 boot > 25s).
Jordan (eng-runtime): I'll push a telemetry build that emits detailed init spans and schedule a canary against a small pool with synthetic warm spikes.
Sam Patel: For immediate mitigation, recommend lowering SLO alert sensitivity threshold for this pool to avoid noisy paging while we tune autoscaler (but only after rollback completes). Also add temporary hard limit on burst acceptance to protect other pools.
Rita Chen: Agreed. I'll create the follow-up ticket and assign owners:
- RCA and infra fix: Jordan, Alex
- Autoscaler tuning: Sam, Maya
- Customer comms & postmortem: Jamie
Ticket: INF-2026-1123 created, link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2026-1123
Jamie (cs): I'll prepare customer notes and send an interim update to affected accounts.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated, severity=high->nearby, affected_customers=3, mitigation_actions=[reroute, prewarm, rollback_canary]. Next update in 2h or on new events.
Rita Chen: wrapping up the live handoff. Oncall rotation: I'm handing to Sam Patel for the remaining rollout checks and to monitor for reoccurrence over the next 2 hours. @Sam Patel +1?
Sam Patel: taking handoff. will watch autoscaler attempts and handshake latency, will escalate if p99 > 1.8s for 10m.
Maya Ops: nice job team. please jot down exact warmup stack traces and kernel timing for the postmortem.
Jordan (eng-runtime): will attach init traces to the ticket.
Rita Chen: thanks all. closing the paging thread. :white_check_mark:
